info.name: HRX × CentroVision Telephony
info.description:
# HRX Telephony Ingest — runnable contract

Everything CentroVision needs to prove their side works before writing a line of production code, and everything Hi Tech Group needs to prove the endpoint is wired up correctly.

## Setup (2 minutes)

1. Open the collection **Variables** tab.
2. Set `base_url` to the UAT host.
3. Set `api_key` and `shared_secret` to the values Hi Tech Group issued you. These arrive separately from this file — never in the same email.
4. Run **1.1 GET /health**. Do not go further until it is green.

## Then

Press **Run collection**. Every request carries assertions, so the run report is the evidence — attach it to the UAT sign-off.

Run folders in order. Section 5 (the negatives) depends on 2.8 having run immediately before, because 5.2 replays its event.

## Signing

The collection-level **Pre-request Script** does the signing. Read it once and you have the whole integration:

```
signable  = timestamp + "." + nonce + "." + raw_body
signature = "sha256=" + hex(HMAC_SHA256(shared_secret, signable))
```

Sign the bytes you are about to send. Do not parse the JSON and re-serialise it before signing — key order and whitespace will differ and every signature will fail. That is the single most common cause of a 401 here.

## The one that matters

**3.1 MANUAL DIAL (UAT-05)** is the go/no-go item. Most integrations of this kind fail because only API-originated calls are reported while half the floor dials manually. If your platform cannot raise that event, say so at kickoff, not at UAT.

exec: //  Runs before every request in this collection. You should not need to edit
//  it -- port the logic to your own language and you have the integration.
// Fresh for every request, except the duplicate-detection test, which has to
// re-send an event_id HRX has already seen. Request 2.8 saves its id and 5.2
// is matched here BY NAME rather than by "whatever runs next" -- the folders
// in between would otherwise consume it, and 5.2 would silently test nothing.
// Decided here, by request name, rather than in a per-request script: a
// request-level pre-request script runs AFTER this one, so anything it set
// would arrive too late for its own request and leak into the next.
// A nonce is remembered for 10 minutes, so it must be fresh per HTTP request
// -- including per retry of the same event_id.
// IMPORTANT: sign the bytes you are about to SEND. replaceIn() resolves the
// {{variables}} exactly as Postman will when it transmits, so the signed
// string and the sent string are identical. Do NOT JSON.parse and re-stringify
// here -- key order and whitespace would differ and the signature would fail.
// pm.variables.get() -- NOT pm.collectionVariables.get() -- so the secret is
// found whether it is set as a collection variable, an environment variable,
// or passed with newman --env-var. Reading the collection scope directly
// silently signs with an empty secret and every request 401s.
console.error('shared_secret is not set. Open the collection Variables tab and paste the secret Hi Tech Group issued you.');
// The negative test for a forged signature sets its own bad value and marks
// itself so this script leaves it alone.

item.name: 3. Manual dial and inbound — THE GO/NO-GO

request.description:
THE TEST THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS INTEGRATION IS TRUSTED.

The agent dialled on the handset. HRX never placed the call, so there is no ref_id and the agent block carries only an extension -- often all a handset dial knows.

Most integrations of this kind fail because only API-originated calls are hooked, while half the floor dials manually. If your platform cannot raise this event, say so now rather than at UAT.

request.description:
Everything valid except the signature. If this returns 202, the signature middleware is not wired up and anyone who obtains the API key can forge call records into an HR system.

Note the timestamp and nonce are still valid -- sending a bad signature with no timestamp would fail on a cheaper check first and prove nothing about the HMAC.

exec: pm.test("reported as duplicate, not written twice", function () {

request.description:
Pins a timestamp an hour old. Proves the freshness window is enforced, which is what stops a captured request being replayed later.

If you see this code in real traffic, your server clock has drifted -- run NTP.

Missing event_id, occurred_at and call_uid. HRX stores the rejected payload anyway so it can be inspected -- quote the request_id and you get a precise answer.

Do NOT retry a 422. It will fail identically.

item.description: If any of these pass when they should fail, stop and fix it before sending real call data.

request.description: Send only the recording_uid, never a playable URL. HRX exchanges it for a short-lived signed URL at play time and streams the bytes through its own permission layer.

Send YOUR computed totals here. HRX stores them verbatim rather than deriving them from the state stream, specifically so the HRX productivity report and your User Session report cannot drift apart and become a support ticket.

Backlog drain only, never live traffic. Max 500 per request.

The second event here deliberately has no event_id, to show that one bad row does not reject the batch -- you get a 207 with a per-item result.

exec: pm.test("good row accepted, bad row rejected, batch not lost", function () {

request.description:
Used to close a gap the nightly reconciliation found. Records need no event_id -- HRX derives a stable one from call_uid, so replaying the same row twice collapses to a single event.

Prefer push. Use this to repair, not as a substitute.
